summary: A satirical piece mocking a government's neglect of public cybersecurity awareness and education, casting fictional officials as bumbling characters in a tragicomedy. It uses invented quotes, dated incidents, and metaphors (ostrich, CyberGodot, digital Titanic) to argue that ignorance leaves citizens exposed to scams and hacks.
one_line: Satirical article lampooning a government's willful ignorance of cybersecurity education through fictional officials, absurd quotes, and theatrical metaphors.
key_facts: Cybersecurity Chief 'John Neverhack' was appointed on the 5th of September, 2023, to lead the nation's cyber fortification.
Neverhack declared, "Cybersecurity is like making a sandwich, anyone can do it!"
Asked about cybersecurity education in schools, Neverhack quipped, "Do schools even use the internet these days?"
Education Minister 'Jane Q. Public' was heard saying, "The best way to deal with a virus is chicken soup, works every time."
An emergency meeting on the 12th of October, 2023, addressed hacked government emails that leaked dull lunch orders.
Officials clung to the belief that "password" is the pinnacle of password complexity.
On the 25th of November, 2023, leaked audio from an anonymous source codenamed "123456" captured Neverhack saying, "Hackers are like unicorns, often talked about, but have you ever seen one?"
A report unveiled on the 3rd of December, 2023, revealed a rise in online scams targeting the elderly and young children.
Public remarked, "People must learn from their mistakes," which ignores that people must first be aware mistakes can be made.
The article uses the ostrich with its head in the sand as the nation's emblematic spirit animal for its stance on cybersecurity awareness.
Leaders are depicted awaiting the mythical 'CyberGodot' to educate the masses, while the populace believes antivirus is to cyber threats what garlic is to vampires.
The article concludes that lack of foresight has become the nation's cyber Achilles heel.
